newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee closes firmer, origin sellers absent.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee closes firmer, origin sellers absent.

text.p: Trade and speculator buying supported robusta coffee futures throughout Thursday but the London market largely lagged behind the rally seen in New York, traders said.
During afternoon trading, benchmark July managed to hold within a chart gap left from Wednesday's high of $1,740 and Tuesday's low of $1,820.
"It's holding, there's been a little bit of trade buying as well and some profit-taking on the upside and nothing really from origin," said one trader.
"If you've got those kind of sellers absent from the market, then you're going to see vacuums," he said, adding that speculators had provided most support.
But although London was firm the pace was still behind that in New York, suggesting that nearby support in the robustas could be stronger than in the arabicas.
"I would say London will hold better than New York on the declines, just as London didn't follow New York as quickly on the upmoves," he said.
At the close July stood $55 higher on the day at $1,765 and September up $45 at $1,785. Volume was on the lighter side at 5,840 lots.
Market sources cited little interest to trade the arbitrage against New York, saying the arabicas volatility had thrown the differential's synchronisation.

Traders said while they were still optimistic and expected prices to drift higher, July might not completely fill its chart gap until next week -- unless New York arabicas could recover its recent steep losses.
